terms.definition: Two or more atoms held together by covalent bonds, acting as one unit.
terms.function: Forms the smallest unit of a substance that keeps its identity.
terms.whereItIs: Each of the four structures in the model.
terms.whyItMatters: Molecules are the building blocks of air, water, food, and DNA.

terms.definition: A bond formed when atoms share a pair of electrons.
terms.function: Holds the atoms of a molecule together as a team.
terms.whereItIs: The rods joining the atoms in each molecule.
terms.whyItMatters: Covalent bonds are what turn separate atoms into a molecule.

terms.definition: The smallest piece of a substance that still acts like that substance.
terms.function: Sets the limit: break a molecule and the substance's identity is lost.
terms.whereItIs: Any whole molecule in the model — intact, it is the substance.
terms.whyItMatters: Explains why substances behave the way they do at the particle level.
